details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorms are evolving along a lee trough in far southwestern ND -- potentially being aided by a passing midlevel wave farther north (evident in WV imagery). An elongated hodograph with clockwise curvature (around 30-40 kt of effective shear) and steep midlevel lapse rates atop lower/middle 60s dewpoints will support organized clusters and supercell structures capable of producing large to very large hail and severe wind gusts. Deep-layer shear oriented perpendicular to the lee trough will initially favor discrete cells, though localized upscale growth into small clusters is possible with time. A watch will be issued shortly

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Visible satellite imagery shows gradually deepening moist convection along the higher terrain in southeast AZ. To the immediate west over the lower desert, a hot, well-mixed boundary layer has developed with steep low/mid-level lapse rates contributing to MLCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg. Latest short-term guidance indicates a gradual increase in storm coverage and intensity from late afternoon into this evening as activity spreads east into the more favorable thermodynamic environment. A westerly low-level wind component currently being observed by the Tucson VWP may aid in some forward propagational characteristics and resultant cold pool organization with severe wind gusts up to 80 mph being the primary hazard
